description: Learn to master unit 2 - inference questions for the Digital SAT through a short concept, a modeled item, and targeted practice.
content:
Unit 2 - Inference — Title & Goal
Learn to master unit 2 - inference questions for the Digital SAT through a short concept, a modeled item, and targeted practice.

Key skill

Read the note and focus on what the question is really asking inside the passage.

  • Locate explicit claims and implicit ideas.
  • Ask: What is the passage mainly doing?
  • Match answers to the most general accurate statement.

Model item

Study how the evidence in the passage supports the correct answer.

Passage — The cafe opened an hour early all week, yet the owner kept the lights off in the patio area each morning.

Question 1. What can most reasonably be inferred about the patio?

  • It was closed during the early hour.
  • It was louder than the main room.
  • It had brighter lights than usual.
  • Customers preferred sitting there.
Keeping lights off suggests the patio was not open to customers → A.

Quick practice

Try these quickly. Eliminate two choices before choosing your answer.

Passage — When the speaker mentions calling her grandfather for ‘the long version,’ she smiles and reaches for a notebook.

Question 2. What is the most reasonable inference about the speaker’s plan?

  • She plans to correct her grandfather.
  • She expects detailed information to write down.
  • She will end the conversation quickly.
  • She avoids discussing the topic.
Notebook + ‘long version’ implies she’ll record details → B.

Passage — The lab assistant labeled the sample ‘B’ but placed it in the tray for ‘A.’

Question 3. What can be inferred?

  • The sample may be misfiled.
  • The tray is empty.
  • Sample B is contaminated.
  • The label will dissolve in water.
Mismatch implies possible misfiling → A.

Next skill

Build on the previous skill. Compare how this question type reads the passage differently.

Note: Locate the exact phrase or sentence that proves your choice.

Another model item

Notice how small wording differences change the best answer.

Passage — A note on the door reads: ‘Back in 15 minutes’ with yesterday’s date.

Question 4. Which inference is best supported?

  • The store closed permanently.
  • The sign was not updated and the owner may be absent for longer.
  • The owner returned exactly 15 minutes later.
  • The sign belongs to a different store.
Outdated sign suggests the time estimate no longer applies → B.

More practice

Aim for accuracy first, then speed. Re-check the evidence that rules out each wrong choice.

Passage — Though he insisted the prototype was ‘only a rough sketch,’ he cleared a spot on the shelf and placed it under a light.

Question 5. Which inference is most reasonable?

  • He is proud of the prototype.
  • He will discard it.
  • He dislikes shelves.
  • The light damages the prototype.

Mixed practice set

These mix multiple skills. Mark the question type before you start, then solve.

Passage — The committee released a summary with three key findings but delayed publishing the raw data for two weeks.

Question 6. Which inference is most supported?

  • The data were lost.
  • Members want to review the raw data before public release.
  • There were no key findings.
  • The summary is unrelated to the data.
